newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Detention extended for former Rwanda premier.
newsitem.headline: Detention extended for former Rwanda premier.

text.p: A tribunal on Rwanda's genocide in 1994 extended the detention of former Rwandan prime minister Jean Kambanda for 30 days on Thursday after he said he had no objection.
Kambanda, one of eight suspects arrested in Kenya last month and handed over to the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, appeared in court in Arusha in a black suit but was not handcuffed.
He introduced himself to the tribunal and said he was 42 years old.

Presiding Judge Laity Kama of Senegal read out a letter from Kambanda, saying he did not want a lawyer to defend him and was not opposed to a 30-day extension of detention as sought by the prosecution.
Kama later extended his detention for 30 days and appointed Josette Kadji as his defence counsel.
Prosecutors said the extra time was necessary due to the case's complexity, difficulties in investigating and the need for a precise indictment against him.
Five other suspects transferred from Kenya last month were due to appear before the court later on Thursday for a hearing on the same prosecution request for an extension of detention.
The six appearing in court were not indicted by the tribunal and are only suspected of having participated in the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates in Rwanda in 1994.
The six were therefore only initially detained for 30 days.

The other five appearing on Thursday include former newspaper editor Hassan Ngeze and Belgian Georges Ruggiu, a former journalist at Rwanda's Radio Television des Milles Collines and the only non-Rwandan detained by the tribunal.

The other three were Sylvain Nsabimana, a former government official in the southern Rwandan city of Butare, Gratien Kabiligi, a former colonel in the army's general staff, and Aloys Ntabakuze, former commander of a commando battalion.
The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda was set up in 1994 to bring to justice leaders of the 1994 genocide sparked by the assassination of military strongman Juvenal Habyarimana.
A total of 21 suspects are held in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha, the tribunal's headquarters. Three trials are now underway and a total of 23 suspects have been indicted.
The tribunal said on Wednesday a former commander in Rwanda's ousted Hutu army has been arrested in the Kenyan port city of Mombasa and transferred to detention in Arusha on Tuesday.
